svg.title: Cache-Aside
svg.desc: Cache-Aside. Read from the cache first; on a miss load from the database and populate the cache. Step 1, Miss: load and cache: Miss: user:42 isn't cached, so the App reads the database (slow) and caches the row with a TTL. Step 2, Hits from the cache: Hits: the next reads of user:42 come straight from the cache in ~1 ms; the database stays idle. Step 3, Write, then invalidate: Write: update the database first, then delete the cache entry instead of overwriting it. Step 4, Miss again, refill: Miss again: the next read misses, as after a TTL expiry, and refills the cache with the new value.

g.text: Miss: user:42 isn't cached, so the App reads the database (slow) and caches the row with a TTL.
Hits: the next reads of user:42 come straight from the cache in ~1 ms; the database stays idle.
Write: update the database first, then delete the cache entry instead of overwriting it.
Miss again: the next read misses, as after a TTL expiry, and refills the cache with the new value.
Lazy loading: a key is cached only once something reads it.
Served from memory until it expires, is deleted or is evicted.
The cached copy is stale until the App deletes it.
Delete, don't overwrite: two writers' SETs
could land out of order and cache the older value.
An expired TTL causes exactly the same miss and refill.
